name: Cameron Highlands vegetable terrace
headline: Cool nights grow Malaysia's cabbages and tomatoes, but cleared slopes send mud into the rivers every monsoon.
story: A 1.2 ha terraced farm on a steep slope near Brinchang growing cabbage back to back with tomato under rain shelters. The cool climate is rare in Malaysia and valuable, but heavy pesticide and fertiliser use, bare beds between crops and 3,000 mm of rain a year drive soil loss and turbid rivers. Clubroot and bacterial wilt build up in soils that never rest from brassicas and nightshades.

baseline_rotation.name: Cabbage - tomato, bare beds between crops
baseline_rotation.note: Sentinel-2 sees two to three short crop cycles a year on these terraces; the crops are typical of the area.

water_context.in_situ_source: JPS river turbidity and suspended sediment, Sungai Bertam
water_context.note: Water is plentiful. The problem is what leaves the farm: sediment, nitrate and pesticide in the Bertam and Telom rivers.

cabbage.note: Collectors truck to Kuala Lumpur and Singapore wholesale markets daily.

tomato.note: Same collectors; premium for rain-shelter fruit.

chili.note: Sold, but highland chili competes with lowland supply.

sweet_corn.note: Tourist stalls along the highland road.
